question.text: Hitler's Nazi Germany carried out this genocide during which over ten million civilians were killed. Among those targeted were Jews, Gypsies, and homosexuals.
question.clue: Norman Finkelstein argues that this event has been improperly appropriated as a source of legitimacy.

swap.leadin: Tsar Nicholas II and this man sent each other a series of ten telegrams in summer 1914 as their countries teetered on the brink of war.
swap.text: Nicholas II corresponded with this man, his cousin and the last Kaiser of Germany.
swap.clue: In an 1897 speech, this leader's foreign minister Bernhard von Bulow outlined how this ruler's nation wanted its "place in the sun."

question.leadin: This city's Burgerbraukeller was the site of an uprising on November 8th, 1923 supported by Erich Ludendorff.
question.text: Name this Bavarian city, the site of Adolf Hitler's failed Beer Hall Putsch.
question.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

swap.leadin: This leader argued that "the great questions of the day will not be decided through speeches and decisions, but by iron and blood."
swap.text: Name this Prussian statesman, known as the Iron Chancellor, whose philosophy of Realpolitik succeeded in unifying Germany in the 19th century.
swap.clue: This man disliked the papacy of Pius IX and the dogma of Papal Infallibility, reacting by abolishing the Catholic Department, inaugurating the Kulturkampf.

question.leadin: This document allowed teachers to be fired indiscriminately and banned secret or unauthorized student groups.
question.text: Name these decrees that were issued following the murder of August von Kotzebue by Karl Sand.
question.clue: The enforcement of one provision forbidding the assembly of the Burschenschaften prompted Wilhelm von Humboldt to resign from politics.

swap.text: This man began the Silesian Wars by invading Silesia after the death of Charles VI and ended them in the Battles of Chotusitz and Hohenfriedberg. He later won the Battle of Rossbach during the Seven Years' War.
swap.answerHtml: Frederick II [or Frederick the Great; or Friedrich II; or Friedrich der Grosse; or Der Alte Fritz; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: This leader led a surprise attack on the Saxons at Hohenfriedberg , reinforcing the Treaty of Breslau.

question.text: The Battle of the Marne led to the failure of this German war plan to knock France out of the war by swinging through a country to its north to capture Paris.
question.clue: This German strategy, named for a former German field marshal, advocated sweeping through France, then transporting troops east to handle the slower-to-mobilize Russian forces.

swap.leadin: Wilhelm Keitel served as the first and only military governor of this region.
swap.text: Name this majority German-speaking territory that was handed over in the Munich Pact, a cession that Neville Chamberlain claimed had brought "peace for our time."
swap.clue: The Munich Agreement allowed the annexation by Nazi Germany of this region of Czechoslovakia historically inhabited by German speakers.

question.text: The investiture controversy was eventually ended by a Concordat signed in this German city. Martin Luther was questioned at a 1521 diet in this city.
question.clue: In this city, a religious reformer stated that his "conscience is captive to the Word of God."

swap.leadin: This politician fell to his knees in repentance in front of Nathan Rapoport's Warsaw Ghetto Uprising memorial.
swap.text: Name this leader of the SDP who secured a 1970 agreement with Poland recognizing the Oder-Neisse Line as the official border. This chancellor launched the Ostpolitik policy.
swap.clue: He recognized the Oder-Neisse Line in a nonaggression treaty with Poland.

question.text: The Battle of Koniggratz was a skirmish in this larger conflict, sometimes called the Seven Weeks War. The ostensible cause of this conflict was the Schleswig-Holstein problem.
question.clue: Either Koniggratz or Sadowa was the most important battle in this war, a decisive victory for the northern belligerents.

swap.text: At this meeting presided over by Charles V, Luther declared "Here I stand, I can do no other" while refusing to renounce his beliefs. After this meeting, Luther fled to Wartburg Castle.
swap.clue: The Holy Roman Emperor sent the Archbishop of Trier, Johannes Eck, to speak before this assembly, which also saw Philip the Magnanimous' first meeting with its central figure.

question.leadin: Answer the following about random titles held by German noblemen.
question.text: This Saxon prince declared himself the first Margrave of Brandenburg before joining the Wendish Crusade with Henry the Lion.
question.clue: This member of the House of Ascania who was the frst Margrave of Brandenburg, and whose vigorous campaign-ing won him an animal epithet.

swap.text: Cistercian monks colonized this German region during an 1168 gold rush in its city of Freiberg (fry-bearg) near the Ore Mountains, which became a center of European mining activity for several centuries.
swap.clue: The House of Wettin ruled this region until its 1918 dissolution, marking the end of king Frederick Augustus III's reign.

question.leadin: This woman was photographed with her friend Herta Schneider and dogs Negus and Katuschka by the photographer Heinrich Hoffmann, and she met her eventual husband while she was working for Hoffmann.
question.text: Name this woman who had twice attempted suicide in her twenties before she used a cyanide capsule to kill herself at age 33.
question.clue: The only time this woman appeared in official press photographs was during the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

swap.text: The Hanse built these trade depots in the ports in which they traded, with examples such as Peterhof in Novgorod, and Steelyard in London.
swap.clue: The fur robe lining likely was exported from Peterhof, one of these trading posts operated by the Hansa. Other examples of these trading posts included the Steelyard in London and Bryggen in Bergen.

question.text: Luther also opposed this group of Anabaptists influenced by Thomas Muntzer. This group, which included Thomas Dreschal and Nicholas Storch, believed themselves to receive messages directly from God.
question.clue: This collective name for three religious agitators whose names were probably Nicholas Storch, Thomas Dreschel, and Marcus Stubner.

swap.text: Eastern Bloc countries often declared "war" on this insect likely spread by WWII. East Germany claimed this "American bug" was biological warfare and had youth groups competitively catch them on "Special Search Days."
swap.answerHtml: Colorado potato beetle [or Lepinotarsa decemlineata; accept the ten-lined spearman; prompt on partial answers]

question.text: This German commander wiped out the Hereros as commander in chief of German South West Africa, by cornering them into the Kalahari Desert, and poisoning their water Kefka-style.
question.answerHtml: Lothar von Trotha (Adrian Dietrich Lothar von Trotha)
question.clue: The Herero Genocide was largely the handiwork of this German commander, who drove the Herero into the desert after the Battle of Waterberg, poisoned their water, and encircled the desert with his soldiers so that they could not escape.

swap.leadin: In Early Modern England, wine from along this non-English river was called hock, named for a town which also pioneered a tall, slim style of bottle.
swap.text: The first mention of the Riesling grape was in the 1435 records of an estate along one of the tributaries of what river?
swap.answerHtml: Rhine River [or Rhein Fluss; prompt on Mosel or Main Rivers by asking “what river does it flow into?”]
swap.clue: Desire to regain lands west of this body of water by a movement headed by Georges Ernest Boulanger led to the first use of the term "revanchism."
